query: In electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD), 'the catch is the physics': kinematical (single-scattering) simulations get Kikuchi band positions right but not intensities, while quantitatively accurate patterns require full dynamical electron diffraction. What is the current state of the art (roughly 2020-2026) for physically accurate dynamical simulation of EBSD/Kikuchi master patterns and their implementations? Please cover: (1) the established dynamical Bloch-wave + Monte Carlo approach used by EMsoft/EMsoftOO (multi-beam dynamical scattering, Monte Carlo electron energy/depth distributions) and any recent methodological refinements; (2) alternative or newer formalisms such as multislice, scattering-matrix/S-matrix, reciprocity-based, or first-principles/DFT-informed scattering-factor approaches for backscatter geometries; (3) machine-learning / neural-network surrogates and GPU-accelerated methods that emulate or speed up dynamical pattern simulation and dictionary indexing; (4) the state of open-source, pure-Python or otherwise easily installable implementations (kikuchipy, diffsims, pyEMsoft, py4DSTEM, abTEM, etc.) and whether any now provide dynamical (not just kinematical) EBSD master patterns; and (5) practical accuracy-vs-cost trade-offs for dictionary indexing of metallic alloys (e.g. Al-Si). Cite specific papers, software, and authors, and note which approaches are production-ready versus research prototypes.
